title: Pauri 24, meaning: no end to praise
hookLine: there is no end to His praise, His works, His gifts; the more is said, the more remains (Japji 24)

cards: Thanking someone who really changed a life is harder than it sounds. A teacher, a grandparent, the friend who showed up when it mattered. You say thank you.
Then you remember something else they did, and something else. You write a card, and the card's too small. The more you say, the more there is to say.
That isn't a failure of your words; it's a sign of how much there was. Pauri 24 is built on that.

teach.h: NO END TO WORKS, GIFTS, SEEING.
teach.b: Pauri 24 is a long chain of the word ant, end. In paraphrase: no end to the praises, no end to telling them. No end to His works, no end to His giving.
No end to seeing, no end to hearing. His mind's purpose can't be known to its end. The created world can't be known to its end, nor its near shore, nor its far one.
So many cry out wanting to find its limits, and its limits can't be found. No one knows this end.
Then the line behind today's carry, in the original: bahutaa aakheeai bahutaa hoe. The more is said, the more there is. That's strange.
Usually saying things uses them up; tell a story and it's told. Here every word of praise opens more to praise.
Then the stanza climbs: great is the Master, high His place, and higher than high is His Name. Only someone as high as He could know Him; only He knows how great He is.
And the last line: Nanak, the gift comes by the glance of grace. That's the stanza's quiet resting point.
Talking can't reach the end. What anyone has comes as a gift, through nadar, grace, a word you'll keep meeting in Japji. So the praising never finishes, and that's not a problem to fix.
In the stanza's terms, that's simply how praise of the endless works.

how: Pauri 24 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; Sikhs often quote bahutaa aakheeai bahutaa hoe to say that praise of the One never runs out.

o: a vow of devotion made before God
grace, a glance that gives unearned
a sharp eye that judges every deed

games.q: what's inside Pauri 24 — tap the pairs.

s: in Pauri 24, praising uses up what there is to say
the more is said, the more there is: bahutaa aakheeai bahutaa hoe.
Pauri 24 says only He knows how great He is
only someone as high as He could know Him.
Pauri 24 ends with the gift coming by grace
Nanak, the gift comes by the glance of grace.

games.q: you've praised and praised, and you still haven't reached the end. what does Pauri 24 say?
o: the more is said, the more there is.
stop, because praise has a limit.
games.why: bahutaa aakheeai bahutaa hoe: every word of praise opens more to praise, and the gift comes by grace.

practice: Pick one thing, a person, a place, the morning light, and praise it silently for one full minute without stopping. When you think you've run out, find one more thing to notice about it, and one more.
Then let the words stop, and sit with what's left over.

wordCard.voice: Nadar, grace, the glance that gives without being earned. No end to the praises, the works, the gifts; the more is said, the more there is; and the gift comes by grace.

orig.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 24: the more is said, the more there is.

carryVoice: Your line: the more remains. Like the card that's too small, it tells you how much there was. That's day two hundred two.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 5 (Japji, Pauri 24, the rest of the stanza)
